욥기-3-1.title: 욥기 3장 1절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-3-1.exegesis: 13. seven days ... nights-- They did not remain in the same posture and without food, &c., all this time, but for most of this period daily and nightly. Sitting on the earth marked mourning ( La 2:10 ). Seven days was the usual length of it ( Ge 50:10 ; 1Sa 31:13 ). This silence may have been due to a rising suspicion of evil in Job; but chiefly because it is only ordinary griefs that find vent in language; extraordinary griefs are too great for utterance.

욥기-3-2.title: 욥기 3장 2절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-3-2.exegesis: CHAPTER 3 THE POEM OR DEBATE ITSELF (Job 3:2-42:6). FIRST SERIES IN IT (Job 3: 1-14:22 ). JOB FIRST ( Job 3:1-26 ). Job 3:1-19 . Job Curses the Day of His Birth and Wishes for Death. 1. opened his mouth-- The Orientals speak seldom, and then sententiously; hence this formula expressing deliberation and gravity ( Psa 78:2 ). He formally began. cursed his day-- the strict Hebrew word for "cursing:" not the same as in Job 1:5 . Job cursed his birthday, but not his God.

욥기-3-3.title: 욥기 3장 3절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-3-3.exegesis: 2. spake-- Hebrew, "answered," that is, not to any actual question that preceded, but to the question virtually involved in the case. His outburst is singularly wild and bold ( Jr 20:14 ). To desire to die so as to be free from sin is a mark of grace; to desire to die so as to escape troubles is a mark of corruption. He was ill-fitted to die who was so unwilling to live. But his trials were greater, and his light less, than ours.

욥기-3-4.title: 욥기 3장 4절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-3-4.exegesis: 3. the night in which-- rather "the night which said." The words in italics are not in the Hebrew. Night is personified and poetically made to speak. So in Job 3:7 , and in Psa 19:2 . The birth of a male in the East is a matter of joy; often not so of a female.

욥기-3-5.title: 욥기 3장 5절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-3-5.exegesis: 4. let not God regard it-- rather, more poetically, "seek it out." "Let not God stoop from His bright throne to raise it up from its dark hiding-place." The curse on the day in Job 3:3 , is amplified in Job 3:4 , 5 ; that on the night, in Job 3:6-10 .

욥기-3-6.title: 욥기 3장 6절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-3-6.exegesis: 5. Let ... the shadow of death-- ("deepest darkness," Is 9:2 ). stain it-- This is a later sense of the verb [Gesenius]; better the old and more poetic idea, "Let darkness (the ancient night of chaotic gloom) resume its rights over light ( Ge 1:2 ), and claim that day as its own." a cloud-- collectively, a gathered mass of dark clouds. the blackness of the day terrify it-- literally, "the obscurations"; whatever darkens the day [Gesenius]. The verb in Hebrew expresses sudden terrifying. May it be suddenly affrighted at its own darkness. Umbreit explains it as "magical incantations that darken the day," forming the climax to the previous clauses; Job 3:8 speaks of "cursers of the day" similarly. But the former view is simpler. Others refer it to the poisonous simoom wind.

욥기-3-7.title: 욥기 3장 7절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-3-7.exegesis: 6. seize upon it-- as its prey, that is, utterly dissolve it. joined unto the days of the year-- rather, by poetic personification, "Let it not rejoice in the circle of days and nights and months, which form the circle of years."

욥기-3-8.title: 욥기 3장 8절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-3-8.exegesis: 7. solitary-- rather, "unfruitful." "Would that it had not given birth to me."
욥기-3-8.theologicalNote: 7. solitary-- rather, "unfruitful." "Would that it had not given birth to me."

욥기-3-9.title: 욥기 3장 9절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-3-9.exegesis: 8. them ... curse the day-- If "mourning" be the right rendering in the latter clause of this verse, these words refer to the hired mourners of the dead ( Jr 9:17 ). But the Hebrew for "mourning" elsewhere always denotes an animal, whether it be the crocodile or some huge serpent ( Is 27:1 ), such as is meant by "leviathan." Therefore, the expression, "cursers of day," refers to magicians, who were believed to be able by charms to make a day one of evil omen. (So Balaam, Nu 22:5 ). This accords with Umbreit's view ( Job 3:7 ); or to the Ethiopians and Atlantes, who "used to curse the sun at his rising for burning up them and their country" [Herodotus]. Necromancers claimed power to control or rouse wild beasts at will, as do the Indian serpent-charmers of our day ( Psa 58:5 ). Job does not say they had the power they claimed; but, supposing they had, may they curse the day. Schuttens renders it by supplying words as follows:--Let those that are ready for anything, call it (the day) the raiser up of leviathan, that is, of a host of evils.

욥기-3-10.title: 욥기 3장 10절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-3-10.exegesis: 9. dawning of the day-- literally, "eyelashes of morning." The Arab poets call the sun the eye of day. His early rays, therefore, breaking forth before sunrise, are the opening eyelids or eyelashes of morning.

욥기-3-13.title: 욥기 3장 13절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-3-13.exegesis: 12. Why did the knees prevent me?-- Old English for "anticipate my wants." The reference is to the solemn recognition of a new-born child by the father, who used to place it on his knees as his own, whom he was bound to rear ( Ge 30:3 ; 50:23 ; Is 66:12 ).

욥기-3-14.title: 욥기 3장 14절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-3-14.exegesis: 13. lain ... quiet ... slept-- a gradation. I should not only have lain, but been quiet, and not only been quiet, but slept. Death in Scripture is called "sleep" ( Psa 13:3 ); especially in the New Testament, where the resurrection-awakening is more clearly set forth ( 1Co 15:51 ; 1Th 4:14 ; 5:10 ).

욥기-3-15.title: 욥기 3장 15절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-3-15.exegesis: 14. With kings ... which built desolate places for themselves-- who built up for themselves what proved to be (not palaces, but) ruins! The wounded spirit of Job, once a great emir himself, sick of the vain struggles of mortal great men, after grandeur, contemplates the palaces of kings, now desolate heaps of ruins. His regarding the repose of death the most desirable end of the great ones of earth, wearied with heaping up perishable treasures, marks the irony that breaks out from the black clouds of melancholy [Umbreit]. The "for themselves" marks their selfishness. Michaelis explains it weakly of mausoleums, such as are found still, of stupendous proportions, in the ruins of Petra of Idumea.

욥기-3-16.title: 욥기 3장 16절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-3-16.exegesis: 15. filled their houses with silver-- Some take this to refer to the treasures which the ancients used to bury with their dead. But see Job 3:26 .
욥기-3-16.theologicalNote: 15. filled their houses with silver-- Some take this to refer to the treasures which the ancients used to bury with their dead. But see Job 3:26 .

욥기-3-17.title: 욥기 3장 17절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-3-17.exegesis: 16. untimely birth-- ( Psa 58:8 ); preferable to the life of the restless miser ( Ec 6:3-5 ).
욥기-3-17.theologicalNote: 16. untimely birth-- ( Psa 58:8 ); preferable to the life of the restless miser ( Ec 6:3-5 ).

욥기-3-18.title: 욥기 3장 18절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-3-18.exegesis: 17. the wicked-- the original meaning, "those ever restless," "full of desires" ( Is 57:20 , 21 ). the weary-- literally, "those whose strength is wearied out" ( Re 14:13 ).
욥기-3-18.theologicalNote: 17. the wicked-- the original meaning, "those ever restless," "full of desires" ( Is 57:20 , 21 ). the weary-- literally, "those whose strength is wearied out" ( Re 14:13 ).

욥기-3-19.title: 욥기 3장 19절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-3-19.exegesis: 18. There the prisoners rest-- from their chains.
욥기-3-19.theologicalNote: 18. There the prisoners rest-- from their chains.

욥기-3-20.title: 욥기 3장 20절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-3-20.exegesis: 19. servant-- The slave is there manumitted from slavery.
욥기-3-20.theologicalNote: 19. servant-- The slave is there manumitted from slavery.

욥기-3-21.title: 욥기 3장 21절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-3-21.exegesis: Job 3:20-26 . He Complains of Life because of His Anguish. 20. Wherefore giveth he light-- namely, God; often omitted reverentially ( Job 24:23 ; Ec 9:9 ). Light, that is, life. The joyful light ill suits the mourners. The grave is most in unison with their feelings.

욥기-3-24.title: 욥기 3장 24절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-3-24.exegesis: 23. whose way is hid-- The picture of Job is drawn from a wanderer who has lost his way, and who is hedged in, so as to have no exit of escape ( Ho 2:6 ; La 3:7 , 9 ).
욥기-3-24.theologicalNote: 23. whose way is hid-- The picture of Job is drawn from a wanderer who has lost his way, and who is hedged in, so as to have no exit of escape ( Ho 2:6 ; La 3:7 , 9 ).

욥기-3-25.title: 욥기 3장 25절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-3-25.exegesis: 24. my sighing cometh before I eat-- that is, prevents my eating [Umbreit]; or, conscious that the effort to eat brought on the disease, Job must sigh before eating [Rosenmuller]; or, sighing takes the place of good ( Psa 42:3 ) [Good]. But the first explanation accords best with the text. my roarings are poured out like the waters-- an image from the rushing sound of water streaming.

욥기-3-26.title: 욥기 3장 26절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-3-26.exegesis: 25. the thing which I ... feared is come upon me-- In the beginning of his trials, when he heard of the loss of one blessing, he feared the loss of another; and when he heard of the loss of that, he feared the loss of a third. that which I was afraid of is come unto me-- namely, the ill opinion of his friends, as though he were a hypocrite on account of his trials.
